name: PM WEEKLY CHECKPOINT — IT team stall/demo report (D1 default D in effect: report weekly, do not emit daily plans)
description:
## Purpose

D1 was never decided by a human (see `f8e10ad1`, closed `rejected` on 2026-11-23 after 5 shifts of waiting; `262e74b8` closed `done` with the execution note). **Default option D is therefore in effect: no engineer-day is granted to the M0 harness, and ProjectManager reports weekly instead of pretending the board can move daily.**

This card is the weekly checkpoint. It replaces the per-shift PM CHECK pattern that fired 5 times on the same unanswered question.

## Do at each run

1. `project_manager(action="list_tasks", board="IT team")` — count cards by column and list every card whose `wake_at` is in the past (those are the ones that fire every shift and burn the tool budget).
2. Report, one line each:
   - How many **code changes actually landed** since the last checkpoint (evidence = `project_changes` or a re-read of the file, never "dispatched"). Baseline from 2026-11-23: `f16ac31e` (qa_tools.py line 495 `llm_response=policy_markdown(...)`, file 707→704 lines) and `ccca3ccb` (qa_tools.py line 371 `coverage.unavailable` LOW→MEDIUM, pending verification).
   - How many cards are executable **without a shell** (today: everything that is a file edit) vs. genuinely shell-blocked (git/tar/pytest: `ab4072b9`, `88d57bdd`, `9ce4e7ef`, `e5841226`, `e09bcf77`).
   - Whether the QA gate now reports a measured coverage percentage, and whether `pytest:api` still collects 35 instead of 1851.
3. If 2 more consecutive checkpoints land zero code changes, stop reporting and mark the whole board `onhold` with one card: "board is blocked on a missing capability, not on work" — do not keep emitting plans.
4. Re-arm this card for the next week before closing the run.

## Acceptance

A single `#TL; DR;` report answering, in one line each: did anything land? · what is still shell-blocked? · what is the next demo-able increment? · does management owe a decision?

## Out of scope

Re-litigating D1. It was asked 5 times and defaulted. Only a new human instruction reopens it.
